item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00015","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C23","C06","C25"],"selected_candidate_label":"C23","confidence":0.96,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C23 is a strong drafting-template candidate because it is an earlier letter to the same recipient and contains the child’s distinctive core conception: Hoover repeatedly undertaking major public responsibilities, the country benefiting from his work, and Eisenhower anticipating the benefit of his recommendations. The birthday letter expands and adapts that material into a broader tribute to Hoover’s career, new governmental assignments, counsel, and judgment. C06 and C25 share similar praise for long public service, repeated assignments, exceptional ability, and continuing counsel, but neither matches the recipient-specific substance as closely as C23.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"after so many years given to the public service, you still cheerfully accept new assignments involving governmental responsibilities of the most burdensome character","parent_excerpt":"The country is to be congratulated that you have once again been willing to undertake leadership in this work.","explanation":"Both praise Hoover for repeatedly accepting substantial new governmental responsibilities despite his already lengthy public career."},{"child_excerpt":"by virtue of your long experience, wise understanding and eminent position, you are qualified, as almost no other American, to discharge them successfully","parent_excerpt":"You have enlisted the services of some of our most outstanding leaders for membership on the task forces that you have established to carry forward these studies.","explanation":"The child generalizes C23’s praise of Hoover’s leadership and capacity to direct nationally important governmental work."},{"child_excerpt":"may we continue to have the benefit of your counsel and judgment","parent_excerpt":"I look forward to having the benefit of your recommendations.","explanation":"This is a close recipient-specific reformulation of the expectation that Eisenhower and the government will continue benefiting from Hoover’s advice."}]}
